rationale: Inherited @NotNull explicitly requires expectedHash. The HTTP parameter annotation omits required; optionality comes from that omission.
The service explicitly takes the supplied refund amount available and forwards it. The field has a dedicated READ_ONLY contract annotation.
The handler explicitly builds SingleReferenceResponse.reference. The operation's response annotation explicitly identifies Reference as the JSON schema.
Both dates pass through requiredInstant, which throws when absent. Operation-specific descriptions explicitly promise default years 1800 and 3000.
The handler explicitly serializes one property object. The list wrapper comes from the response class reused by collection and individual retrieval, rather than dedicated single-item prose.
Status is dereferenced without a null check before transition validation. The status map falls back to 500. The dedicated transition schema requires status and the operation lists 400.

Successful modification explicitly constructs NO_CONTENT. The contract separately specifies 201 with Subjects for creation and 204 for updates; this does not establish that every modification violates the contract.
The search handler deliberately returns SearchMandateResponse with results, counts, page and links. Its operation-specific response annotation instead names MandateResponse.
A GET search mapping explicitly binds a required name parameter. The contract has no dedicated /secrets/search operation; X is an absence, not a stated prohibition.
Unsupported format parsing throws before the handler's try block. The escape is an ordering oversight; the operation explicitly describes 422 for invalid consumer configuration.

The endpoint passes null through to return-URL construction, which dereferences the request. This broken argument flow does not evidently target failed session creation; the operation explicitly promises successful authenticated sessions.
The installed-package service result is explicitly returned as DevicePackages. The GET operation's dedicated annotation specifies DeviceSnapshots despite its package-oriented prose.
assetIds.stream() has no absent-list handling. Optionality is a generated interface's required=false declaration, without dedicated absent-parameter behavior or a default list.
Integer field and getter explicitly choose the implementation's score type. The string claim comes from the shared Project schema, without prose explaining a string representation.

Date fields plus write-dates-as-timestamps=true explicitly select timestamp serialization. The int32 width comes from the reusable ImportJob schema rather than an operation-specific encoding statement.
The handler explicitly requires office; the helper rejects null or empty values. The operation's prose explicitly promises the user-session default.

Missing input triggers requireNotNull, but fold only recovers typed validation errors; no throwable-to-400 handling is supplied here. The escape, rather than input rejection itself, is accidental. The operation explicitly declares JSON validation failures.
Nullable persist is passed to a primitive boolean parameter without null handling, causing unboxing failure. The Bridge field explicitly declares nullable:true.
Creation explicitly returns a status-only ResponseEntity with CREATED. The corresponding operation explicitly specifies a JSON SubmodelElement in its 201 response.
The identifier override reads CLOB_ID, whose value is clob-id. This wrong-constant use conflicts with dedicated prose explaining that blob-id overrides the path identifier.

The existing-artifact helper lacks name and description arguments, so update branches cannot forward those headers. Their omission is not an explicit metadata-suppression policy. The contract dedicates descriptions to both headers.

Duplicate errors are wrapped without conflict status and forwarded unchanged. Missing conflict translation is visible; ⚠️ the writer's 500 outcome is inferred because its implementation is absent. The operation explicitly lists 409.
Optional.of rejects absent dates before the intended orElse(now) defaults. Both query parameters explicitly declare required:false and describe their applicability to the named OpenShift products.
The handler explicitly formats a RecentValue list with RecentValue.class. Its operation-specific response annotation explicitly chooses an array of Tsv.

The backend appends without checking duplicates; 201 then follows the normal creation path. No duplicate-specific acceptance branch exists. The 409 annotation repeats boilerplate about Submodels and SubmodelElements on this reference endpoint.

The exception mapper explicitly assigns BAD_REQUEST to CommitStateUnknownException. The replace-view response explicitly describes server-side commit uncertainty under 500 with that exception example.
The JSON-annotated final boolean explicitly fixes public-client to true. The string/name interpretation resides in the reusable configuration schema, not separate operation-specific behavior.

Y is not established as stated: the 204 branches test missing versions, not unavailable descriptor types. The contract's 404 description explicitly concerns the specified type; descriptor filtering follows a different path.

The converter explicitly throws IllegalArgumentException for unmatched values. The enum is shared and 400 references a shared error response. Throwing alone does not establish a different HTTP status; framework wrapping is outside the shown converter.
The serialized data model explicitly uses BigDecimal. The integer claim is inferred from an Integer field in a Swagger documentation DTO, without dedicated integer-only prose.

The dedicated documentation annotation names _links, but no serialization rename accompanies getLinks. The links output follows bean naming by default; the missing JSON annotation does not evidently target that discrepancy.
Implementation explicitly converts roles into a scope-to-name map. The list shape comes from MemberEntity, the shared response model referenced by the operation.
@RequestBody explicitly requires the Secret entity on PUT. The contract's PUT omits requestBody entirely, so X derives from silence rather than dedicated optional-body prose.
The route configuration explicitly selects singular water-user. The operation annotation explicitly declares the plural water-users path.
After updating Asset Information, the handler explicitly returns OK. The matching contract response explicitly specifies 204 for this update.

The deferred result explicitly completes with a CREATED response carrying Tan. The contract exposes DeferredResult framework properties as a schema, indicating generated wrapper leakage rather than dedicated payload prose.
The GUID branch passes through a service response explicitly constructed with CREATED and a token body. The contract explicitly specifies 200 for GUID/TeleTAN success.

The converter is built once for a connection-cached endpoint; subsequent request content types do not refresh it. Format reuse follows stale cached state. The operation explicitly offers both request media types.
After storing the file, the handler explicitly returns OK. The attachment upload operation explicitly documents 204 for success.

Validation accepts blank or absent dates, then both arguments reach ZonedDateTime.parse without defaults. The optionality flags are bare generated query declarations without dedicated absent-date semantics.
Class-level route and POST mapping explicitly register /api/v1/rating/product. The contract explicitly places this operation under /api/v1/products/rating.
The selected basin is explicitly placed in singletonList before list serialization. The individual-retrieval response annotation explicitly selects a Basin object for JSON without the array flag.
The mapper explicitly assigns BAD_REQUEST to CommitStateUnknownException. The table-update operation explicitly describes 500 for server-side commit uncertainty with that exception example.
The deletion handler explicitly has void return type and supplies no entity. The operation annotation explicitly associates its 204 response with application/json RoleEntity.

An explicit error-result branch serializes error_code and message into offsets. The contract shape comes from shared OffsetRecordSent schemas; they do not require partition/offset or forbid additional fields, so incompatibility is not established.
Deserialization explicitly targets a command with Map<String,Boolean>. The extra map level comes from the Swagger documentation DTO's generic type declaration, without prose requiring nested values.

The service explicitly reads Boolean permission values and unboxes them for role updates. The string claim comes from a Swagger DTO field with a string example of true, rather than dedicated string-value prose.
The empty-tags branch explicitly returns Response.ok().build() without an entity. The matching operation explicitly specifies DomainTagModelList as its JSON 200 payload.
@JsonProperty explicitly chooses payment_id, and the response unwraps that Payment. The camel-case property is a documentation model field, without dedicated naming prose.

Both converters explicitly select null for absent Kafka values. Non-null string behavior derives from the reusable ConsumerRecord type and absent nullable declaration, not explicit tombstone handling prose.
Inherited @NotNull explicitly requires expectedHash for deletion. The HTTP parameter annotation omits required; X is based on that omission.

The anchored regex is checked with find; dollar can match before a terminal line feed. That acceptance is an anchor/matching side effect, not explicit newline handling. Operation prose specifically requires a SHA-256 hashed GUID.
Inherited @NotNull explicitly requires expectedHash for merge. The HTTP parameter declaration omits required, rather than explicitly promising a missing-hash behavior.
Lowercasing is inconsistent with the mixed-case allowed set, unintentionally rejecting listed attributes. Dedicated contract prose and examples explicitly permit averageRating and reviewsCount.

The JSON converter explicitly parses value bytes into JsonNode and inserts that structure. The string claim comes from the shared ConsumerRecord schema; JSON-format examples elsewhere in this item's contract already show structured values.

The ZIP branch returns a streaming entity with only Content-Disposition; no media type is assigned there. This is a header omission. The operation explicitly offers application/zip and describes format=zip.

The existing-artifact helper drops dryRun and eventually hardcodes false for version creation. The defect is lost flag propagation, without a dry-run-specific persistence branch. Dedicated contract prose explicitly forbids changes when dryRun=true.

An explicit null-status guard constructs 400. The query declaration explicitly marks status optional and supplies default available; Y concerns a null bound argument, not proof that omission bypasses framework defaulting.

Validation explicitly selects ISO alpha-two parsing with an en/cy error message. ENGLISH/WELSH comes from the referenced request model's enum metadata, which conflicts with its own en example and ISO-code description.
The filter reads DESIGNATOR instead of DESIGNATOR_MASK, a wrong-constant use. Dedicated operation prose explicitly describes designator-mask as the designator filter.
CASE_INSENSITIVE is explicitly enabled for state validation. The operation's query parameter explicitly publishes a lowercase-only regex without that flag.
The handler explicitly constructs JsonGenericResponseMessage from the generic device response. Its operation annotation explicitly specifies DeviceCommandOutput as the response model.
The class route plus GET suffix explicitly forms /api/v1/rating/product/{productId}. The contract explicitly declares /api/v1/products/rating/{productId}.
The update code explicitly reads a Long parameter named value and assigns it. The numeric description name comes from a Swagger documentation DTO field, without explanatory naming prose.
Inherited @NotNull explicitly requires expectedHash for transplant. The HTTP parameter declaration omits required; X derives from an unspecified flag.

The identifier branch explicitly writes one identity and returns early. The operation links a dedicated listIdentities response whose schema explicitly specifies an array, without a single-object alternative.

Sorting inputs are bound but never applied while predicates, offset and limit are applied. This is omitted query configuration. The ordering promise is inherited from shared sortParam and sortDir parameter definitions.

The parser explicitly converts submitted metadata entries directly into a map and constructs ExternalMetadata. The nested-map claim derives from the reusable ExternalMetadata schema referenced by request metadata, without dedicated nested-input prose.

The selected formatter produces the body, but its media type is never assigned; servlet defaults remain. This is an omitted header assignment. The operation explicitly advertises the office representation media types.
The metrics handler explicitly sends the scrape body with 200 but omits Content-Type. The missing header is an omission; the operation explicitly specifies text/plain for success.
